title: The two Vietnams

draft.title: The two Vietnams
card: A communist state led by Ho Chi Minh, with its capital at Hanoi. It aimed to unite all of Vietnam under communist rule.
A non-communist state with its capital at Saigon. It was backed by the United States, which supported it against communism.
Communist guerrillas who lived in the South and fought the Southern government. They were supported by the North.
So the conflict was not only North against South. Within the South, the government also faced a war against its own communist opponents.
draft.remember: The North was communist and the South was US-backed, and the Viet Cong fought the Southern government from inside the South.

opts: Communist fighters in the South who opposed its government
The regular army of the Southern government
American soldiers sent to defend Saigon
Political leaders who governed North Vietnam from Hanoi
a.why: The Viet Cong were communists living in South Vietnam who fought the Southern government, with support from the North. They are easily mistaken for the North's own leaders, but those governed from Hanoi and were not fighters inside the South.
a.clue: Think about where they lived and who they fought.

b.q: In 1962, a village in South Vietnam is attacked by guerrillas who live in the countryside nearby and oppose the Saigon government. Which description fits the attackers best?
opts: Viet Cong fighting the Southern government
Soldiers of the US-backed Southern government
Civil servants of Ho Chi Minh's government in Hanoi
Foreign troops invading from outside Vietnam
b.why: Guerrillas who lived in the South and opposed the Saigon government match the Viet Cong. The attackers were not the Southern government's own soldiers, as those were the force the guerrillas fought against.
b.clue: Which group lived in the South but opposed its government?

a.best: Communist fighters in the South who opposed its government

b.best: Viet Cong fighting the Southern government
